text:
ana: Heads up — I found an issue with the daily billing export to BigQuery. Looks like the invoice_description field is being truncated at 255 chars which is causing our heuristic matcher to attribute usage rows to the wrong customer.

kevin: Oof. Is that the new export_v2 pipeline?

ana: yes, export_v2. The ETL step that writes to BQ does `LEFT(description, 255)` before ingest. Mira and I noticed multiple rows with the same truncated description but different Stripe invoice IDs.

mira: example rows from staging: 
```
invoice_id: inv_1A2b3C, customer_id: cus_ABC, description: "Enterprise plan — 50 users — promo: summer-launch-2025-long-description-...(full text 600 chars)"
invoice_id: inv_9X8y7Z, customer_id: cus_DEF, description: "Enterprise plan — 50 users — promo: summer-launch-2025-long-description-...(different tail but same first 255 chars)"
```
both get truncated to the same 255 prefix and our downstream join by description+amount collapses them.

devon: How many invoices affected? Any revenue impact yet?

mira: Preliminary query: `SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT invoice_id) as invoices, COUNT(*) as imported_rows FROM analytics.billing_export WHERE LENGTH(original_description) > 255 AND export_date >= DATE_SUB(CURRENT_DATE(), INTERVAL 30 DAY);` returned ~ 42 invoices in last 30d where truncation happened. Matching collisions caused ~15 misallocations by the reports team.

kevin: Can we re-run the ingest with the full description? Is Stripe returning full description if we expand lines?

ana: Yes — Stripe API includes full line descriptions. The quick mitigation is to switch the BQ schema to store `full_description STRING` and stop relying on truncated text for joins. Also we should switch downstream matching to use `stripe_invoice_id` instead of description+amount.

mira: Temporary patch I tested in staging: remove the `LEFT(description, 255)` and write the full description into `invoice_description_full`. SQL diff I ran: 
```
-- before
INSERT INTO analytics.billing_export (invoice_id, customer_id, invoice_description, amount)\nSELECT id, customer, LEFT(description,255), total FROM stripe_export;
-- after
INSERT INTO analytics.billing_export (invoice_id, customer_id, invoice_description_full, amount)\nSELECT id, customer, description, total FROM stripe_export;
```
Worked in staging.

billing-bot: Scheduled job `billing-export-v2` failed 2024-06-12 03:12:05 UTC: schema mismatch (column invoice_description length).

devon: Plan: 1) Patch export job to write full_description 2) Update downstream matching to prefer invoice_id joins 3) Reprocess last 60 days into a new table `billing_export_reprocessed` and run reconciliation 4) Deploy fix and monitor.

ana: I'll create a finance incident ticket and mark priority P2. Can eng-data pick up the reprocess?

kevin: I'll own the export change and reprocess. Will run in a sandbox BQ dataset first, run the reconciliation query Mira wrote, then promote. ETA EOD tomorrow.

mira: I'll provide the reconciliation SQL and a list of affected customers to outreach to if needed.

ana: Quick workaround for now: do not use description matching in any current ad-hoc reports. I'll ping ops/docs.

devon: Also add a unit test to the ETL that fails if we ever call LEFT(description, 255) again 🙂

ana: Thanks — assigning ticket FIN-BILL-312. Devon, please add the test requirement.

kevin: starting the sandbox run now. I'll post results here. :eyes:

mira: thanks, will stand by for the reconciliation output.

kevin: sandbox reprocess completed. Reconciliation shows 14 misallocations fixed, no net revenue change, just corrected customer attribution. Ran a quick outreach draft for affected accounts.

ana: Perfect. Closing the loop: export_v2 will be updated to include invoice_id in all downstream joins and store full descriptions. Reprocess for last 60 days done. Will follow up with a postmortem next week. :thumbsup:
